question:
Improve telemetry (clarity and design)

[PostHog's strategy](https://posthog.com/handbook/strategy) is to focus everything we have for at least the next 6-12 months (and likely, beyond that), on making the Community Edition awesome and very popular.

PostHog currently uses PostHog to track itself where users haven't opted themselves out.

We believe tracking Daily Active Users is the most meaningful top metric to check if we are achieving our strategy. That's because it's the combination of (i) new users signing up and (ii) existing users sticking around.

We currently have basic telemetry in the product for **non-opted out** users (anyone can opt out at any time). We use PostHog to track the following:

* new PostHog user signed up - name, email and company name entered
  * = used to produce unique sign ups
* pageviews for PostHog users when they come back to the product
  * = used to produce DAUs

The challenge

There is no fine grained control for users over this telemetry:

* You can opt out of nothing or everything, and the opt out is on the /settings page where most users go to set up the product
* If a single user opts out, they opt out of (i) aggregated data (ii) identifiable data (ii) their entire team

This means almost every engaged user that we know of anecdotally has (understandably) opted out of our tracking.

We also are not clear over exactly how our telemetry works (we have just moved docs and need to add a new section for this - legacy [explanation](https://docs.posthog.com/#/product-direction)), and should clarify things. For example, if it is left on, we do not collect users' user data, which is probably important for people to know :)

Proposal

I would like us to (i) make it easier to remove personally identifiable information from our tracking but (ii) make it more likely people leave anonymized "counter" style tracking to let us assess page views properly.

There are several conditions that we would need to meet for this to be responsible:

* If a user is opted out, that user shall forever remain opted out of everything
* We should explain clearly in our new docs what the telemetry does
* We should raise this in the community first to give people a chance to talk about it

To solve this, I'd suggest:

1. we create a page somewhere that is specific to our telemetry in the app, as the regular settings page is becoming complex Ie setup>advanced.

* That page makes clear exactly what is tracked and what isn't.
* This page lets you opt out of the data categories we track in a more fine-grained way:
  * Team level (ideally this would only come from an admin role)
  * User and field level

2. We track anonymized aggregated usage information by default, but provide a code level change to manage this, that we would explain how to do in the docs. Just the minimum info would be collected to work out anonyized DAUs. I'd see that as the only cost of the free software, which helps us keep raising money and building cool stuff.

Why I think this is the right direction

If PostHog can track DAUs, we're much better able to explain the software's popularity to investors. There is significant social good in this - it lets us build a powerful, stable and well supported product and community.

However, our mini group of employees are not the only people in the community and I want to get feedback from anyone reading this before implementing it. Do you agree? Else, could you suggest a different approach to the challenge above?
issue_title: Improve telemetry (clarity and design)

question:
LLM Analytics: trace view duplicates generations and inflates totals when events lack $ai_span_id

The LLM Analytics **trace view** renders the same generation multiple times and inflates the trace's token/cost totals, for traces whose `$ai_generation` events have no `$ai_span_id`.

**Observed** (PostHog Cloud US, project 222862):

- Trace `caption-chat-kh7ayjbhs3wdf7thdjh2f2avqn8a78za-1783636807880` shows **two** identical generation nodes in the tree (gpt-5-mini, 582→353 tokens, 3.9s each) and a header of `1164 → 706 (Σ 1870)` — exactly 2× the real single call.
- The `events` table contains **exactly one** `$ai_generation` event for that trace id (verified via HogQL) — so insights/cost dashboards are correct; only the trace view inflates.
- The trace-content store has **three** rows for that trace: `SELECT count(), countDistinct(span_id) FROM posthog.ai_events WHERE trace_id = '...'` → `3, 0` (all rows have empty `span_id`).

How we produce the events

`@posthog/ai` **8.3.0** `withTracing` wrapping a Vercel AI SDK model (`generateObject`), with `posthogTraceId`/`posthogDistinctId`/`posthogProperties` set. This wrapper does not emit `$ai_span_id` (grepping the published package, span ids appear only in the langchain and openai-agents integrations).

Root-cause hypothesis

Ingestion into the trace-content store is at-least-once, and with `span_id` empty there is no dedup key — so retried deliveries land as extra rows, and the trace tree renders one node per row (and sums their tokens/cost in the header).

Suggested fixes (either would resolve it)

1. Dedup rows in the trace-content store when `span_id` is absent (e.g. by event uuid), or dedup at trace-view query time.
2. Emit a `$ai_span_id` per generation from the Vercel AI SDK wrapper in `@posthog/ai`, matching the langchain/openai-agents integrations.

Happy to provide more event uuids / timestamps from our project if useful.
issue_title: LLM Analytics: trace view duplicates generations and inflates totals when events lack $ai_span_id

question:
Workaround Needed for Cookie Validation Issue During Django Upgrade

We've encountered an issue related to two-factor authentication cookie validation after a major Django version upgrade, as detailed in issue [#686](https://github.com/jazzband/django-two-factor-auth/issues/686). This issue arises due to the change in user password hashes when Django's hash iteration count is updated in a new version, leading to a mismatch in the two-factor authentication cookies' validation.

We can for now implement a workaround. This involves catching the `BadSignature` exception raised during the cookie validation process when there's a mismatch in the hashes. This situation occurs after upgrading Django, which causes the user's password hash to change, thereby invalidating the existing two-factor authentication cookies.

This issue is critical for us to upgrade our Django version without disrupting the user experience of people coming back and having a 2FA cookie.
issue_title: Workaround Needed for Cookie Validation Issue During Django Upgrade

question:
Log-alert destinations cannot be edited (Save / per-kind toggle fail; alert API has no update)

There is no supported way to **edit** a log-alert notification destination after create. The UI still presents an editor, per-kind Active switches, and copy that says you can change headers / body / filters. Every write goes to the generic hog-functions API and is rejected:

> Alert notification destinations are managed through the alert API.

The alert destinations API that message points at only supports **create** and **delete of the whole HogFunction group**. It cannot update URL, headers, enabled flags, or which event kinds notify.

That is the product bug. Save / toggle failures are the UI hitting a write path that does not exist.

Example Cloud pages (EU, project `117388`, alert `workers`):

- Alert notifications: https://eu.posthog.com/project/117388/logs/alerts/01a04724-65dc-743b-ac2f-18bb68cfb5ab/notifications/01a04727-73b8-0000-bcca-5b895ab35403
- HogFunction editor (Save): https://eu.posthog.com/project/117388/functions/01a04727-73b8-0000-bcca-5b895ab35403?returnTo=%2Flogs%2Falerts%2F01a04724-65dc-743b-ac2f-18bb68cfb5ab%2Fnotifications%2F01a04727-73b8-0000-bcca-5b895ab35403

1. Logs → Alerts → open an alert that has a webhook destination → Notifications → open the destination.
2. Toggle **Active** on Firing (or Resolved / Auto-disabled / Errored).
3. Toast: `Failed to pause notification: Alert notification destinations are managed through the alert API.` Switch snaps back to Active.
4. Click **Open editor**. Page copy: *"These hog functions only run for this alert. Open one to edit the message body, headers, filters, or destination details…"*
5. Change Headers (e.g. add `Authorization`) or any other field → **Save**.
6. Trigger field shows the same validation error; Save does not persist. `PATCH /api/projects/:id/hog_functions/:id/` with `{ "enabled": false }` or `{ "inputs": … }` returns the same 400 (`field: filters`).
7. `POST /api/projects/:id/hog_functions/` with `type=internal_destination`, `template-webhook`, and `$logs_alert_firing` + `alert_id` is rejected the same way.
8. `POST /api/projects/:id/logs/alerts/:id/destinations/` accepts only `type` + Slack fields or `webhook_url`. No `headers`, `enabled`, or `event_kinds`. Always creates all four kinds. No destination `PATCH`. Delete is atomic for the whole group.

**Why this is one issue.** [#84149](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/84149) (closed) and [#84285](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/84285) fixed **reads** of managed destinations. The write guard was called deliberate. The leftover hole is: users still need to change a destination, and nothing can.

**What users cannot do today (all the same gap):**

| Need | Blocked by |
| --- | --- |
| Custom webhook headers (Bearer / HMAC) | Create hardcodes `WEBHOOK_HEADERS` (`Content-Type`, `X-PostHog-Webhook-Version: 1`) in `products/alerts/backend/destination_configs.py`. Hog-functions PATCH refused. |
| Firing-only (skip resolved / errored / auto-disabled) | `create_destination` always loops `EVENT_KINDS`. Cannot delete one kind. Cannot `enabled: false` one HogFunction. |
| Pause / resume one kind | LemonSwitch → `api.hogFunctions.update({ enabled })` → write guard. |
| Change URL / body / filters in place | No destination update. Terraform provider documents the same: delete + recreate, with a window of no notifications. |

**Where the UI lies**

- `LogsAlertNotificationDetailScene.tsx` — per-kind `logs-alert-destination-toggle-*` → `setHogFunctionEnabled` → `api.hogFunctions.update`.
- `logsAlertNotificationDetailSceneLogic.ts` — lists via `api.hogFunctions.list`; toggle/save never call the alert destinations API.
- HogFunction configuration Save → `submitConfiguration` → same hog-functions PATCH.
- Insight-alert destinations *can* be edited via hog-functions because `$insight_alert_firing` is carved out of `is_managed_alert_internal_event`. `$logs_alert_*` is not.

**Write guard** (`products/cdp/backend/api/hog_function.py`): any create/update whose filters include a managed `$…_alert_(firing\|resolved\|errored\|auto_disabled\|match)` event is refused unless `allow_managed_alert_destination` is set. Only the logs alert destinations **create** path sets that flag.

**Alert destinations API surface** (`products/logs/backend/presentation/views/alerts_api.py`):

- `POST …/logs/alerts/:id/destinations/` — create only (`LogsAlertCreateDestinationSerializer`: `type`, slack_*, `webhook_url`).
- `POST …/logs/alerts/:id/destinations/delete/` — atomic group delete.
- `GET …/destinations/` (if shipped) — read.
- No `PATCH` / update.

Related: [#84149](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/84149) (read exclusion, closed), [#84285](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/84285) (GET destinations), [terraform `posthog_logs_alert_destination`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/PostHog/posthog/latest/docs/resources/logs_alert_destination) ("PostHog has no update endpoint for destinations"). [#45336](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/45336) is about having log alerts at all, not editing destinations.

**Suggested direction**

1. Add destination **update** on the alert API (the only writer the guard allows): at least `webhook_url`, custom headers, and which event kinds are enabled (or per-kind `enabled`). Keep create/delete atomic if the group invariant still matters.
2. Point the notifications UI (Save, Active switches, editor) at that API instead of `api.hogFunctions.update`.
3. Until then, hide or disable Save / Open editor / per-kind toggles and drop the "edit headers" copy so the UI matches the API.

A custom / non-managed HogFunction cannot subscribe to `$logs_alert_*` either: the CDP internal-event consumer only invokes a function whose filters include the exact event id plus `alert_id`, and creating that filter is what the write guard blocks.
issue_title: Log-alert destinations cannot be edited (Save / per-kind toggle fail; alert API has no update)

question:
'Matching events' when using 'Element matches HTML selector' in Actions lies to users

The string you put in the `Element matches HTML selector` section of actions is just searched among the elements chain in ClickHouse. This makes sense! Parsing and selecting based on CSS at read time across all events in CH would be too slow.

The problem is that it lies to users, they see `Matching events` and get confused when their action doesn't fire (often they are expecting a Webhook send).

In the example above, the user entered `foo`, thinking it would hit elements with the `foo` class in their HTML. They see matches, are happy, and hit save. The problem is that a plain string CSS selector searches for *elements*, i.e. `<foo>`, to select a class they needed to put `.foo`. Nothing will actually match and the action won't fire.

Our CSS selector logic [is already implemented in TypeScript in the plugin-server](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/72b7077ecf497ef231c67a009776c40fd34d5f0d/plugin-server/src/worker/ingestion/action-matcher.ts#L470). What if we shared the code with the frontend and filtered out matching events on the front-end? It wouldn't be perfect, but it would avoid these common false positives.

Alternatively, or in addition to, we could have a very loud message/banner near `Matching events` when the CSS selector is non-empty.
issue_title: 'Matching events' when using 'Element matches HTML selector' in Actions lies to users

question:
Bug report: data warehouse - dot notation on Parquet struct columns throws errors

Please describe
When a custom S3/GCS source uses Parquet files with native struct columns, PostHog's schema detector correctly identifies the nested structure and labels them as `JSON` type in the UI. However, ClickHouse reads Parquet structs as `Tuple` types internally, and HogQL's dot notation desugars to `JSONExtractRaw()`, which only operates on JSON strings. This means dot syntax like `customer.email` fails with:

> The first argument of function JSONExtractRaw should be a string containing JSON, illegal type: Tuple(...)

The expected behavior is that dot notation on these columns should work, since the schema UI shows them as JSON and the docs describe dot notation as the way to access nested data.

1. Upload a Parquet file to S3 where one or more columns contain native Parquet struct types (not serialized JSON strings).
2. Link it as a custom source in the data warehouse.
3. Observe the struct column shows as `JSON` type in the schema UI.
4. Run a query using dot notation on that column, e.g. `SELECT customer.email FROM my_table LIMIT 1`.
5. Query fails with the `JSONExtractRaw` / `illegal type: Tuple(...)` error.

`tupleElement(customer, 'email')` works as a workaround, confirming ClickHouse can access the data.
From: https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/58028 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/58982)
issue_title: Bug report: data warehouse - dot notation on Parquet struct columns throws errors

question:
Bug: Sorting by person display name breaks tables

Sorting any standard table, i.e. Activity page, by person will break the query:

It happens because we try to sort by `person_display_name` but the select for that hasn't been named in the query:

```sql
SELECT
    tuple(uuid, event, properties, timestamp, team_id, distinct_id, elements_chain, created_at),
    event,
    tuple(coalesce(toString(person.properties.email), toString(person.properties.Email), toString(person.properties.name), toString(person.properties.Name), toString(person.properties.username), toString(person.properties.Username), toString(person.properties.UserName), distinct_id), toString(person.id)),
    coalesce(properties.$current_url, properties.$screen_name),
    properties.$lib,
    timestamp
FROM
    events
WHERE
    and(less(timestamp, toDateTime('2025-05-27 10:41:34.461807')), greater(timestamp, toDateTime('2025-05-26 10:41:29.462900')))
ORDER BY
    person_display_name ASC
LIMIT 101
OFFSET 0
```

A quick solution to that would be to name the select for person_display_name, like this:

```sql
SELECT
    tuple(uuid, event, properties, timestamp, team_id, distinct_id, elements_chain, created_at),
    event,
    tuple(coalesce(toString(person.properties.email), toString(person.properties.Email), toString(person.properties.name), toString(person.properties.Name), toString(person.properties.username), toString(person.properties.Username), toString(person.properties.UserName), distinct_id), toString(person.id)) as person_display_name,
    coalesce(properties.$current_url, properties.$screen_name),
    properties.$lib,
    timestamp
FROM
    events
WHERE
    and(less(timestamp, toDateTime('2025-05-27 10:32:30.311190')), greater(timestamp, toDateTime('2025-05-26 10:32:25.312319')))
ORDER BY
    person_display_name ASC
LIMIT 101
OFFSET 0
```

1. Go to any standard UI table like Activity: https://us.posthog.com/project/150522/activity/explore
2. Click the 3-dot for Person and choose a sorting method

From: https://posthoghelp.zendesk.com/agent/tickets/31165 (moved to PostHog: https://us.posthog.com/project/2/support/tickets/33034)
